title: Agent workflow
body: A person states a task in words. An agent edits the JSON, runs `docc validate` and fixes what it reports, then runs `docc build`. The person reads the generated Markdown and checks meaning and readability, and CI or the pre-commit hook runs `docc check` before the merge. ^egwg

The skill in `skills/docc/SKILL.md` teaches an agent the format, the loop, the diagnostics and the rules of conduct. The main rule: fix the cause of a diagnostic instead of hiding it with `docIgnore`, and link only to ids that exist. ^4vsk

When DOC209 reports a link whose target changed, the agent reads the change the message shows, brings the linking place in line with the target if needed and then writes the hash of the target as it is now into that link by hand; each link is checked on its own and no command confirms links in bulk. DOC402 works the same way for the fingerprint of a code file or region and the documents it points to. The agent never touches a block code: it writes a block it adds without one and `docc build` gives it a code. ^mxan

A review comment on the Markdown is applied to the sources by the agent or by a person, never to `docs/out`. A merge conflict in `docs/out` is resolved by running `docc build`; a conflict in a source file shows up as DOC101 and is resolved first; a conflict over the hash of a link is resolved by checking the place again and writing the hash of the target as it is now. ^5fw7
The commands are described in [[commands@22v9]] and the rules in [[rules@kvpj]]. ^j598
limit: Reachability checks only the shape of the graph. Whether a link means something is left to the reviewer; a version hash only shows that a linked text changed and forces someone to look. ^nbt5
